**Instructions.** Choose the single best answer (a–e) for each question. You may use a periodic table.
Calculators are allowed. Answers are rounded to the precision shown. Time yourself: aim for about 30 minutes
(roughly 2 minutes per question, the same pace as the full exam). The strong-acid and strong-base lists are **not** provided: work from memory.

**Answer sheet.** Use the bubble answer sheet (`CHEM1301/exam-prep/answer-sheet/answer-sheet.pdf`), rows 1–15.

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**1.** According to the course, a **strong acid** is a substance that:

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ is very concentrated\
b)\ forms a precipitate with any metal ion\
c)\ only partially dissociates in water\
d)\ produces OH^−^ ions in water\
e)\ completely dissociates (ionizes) in water, each molecule breaking into an H^+^ ion and an anion

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**2.** Which substance is **neither** a strong acid **nor** a strong base?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ HNO~2~\
b)\ NaOH\
c)\ KOH\
d)\ HCl\
e)\ HNO~3~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**3.** What **salt** forms when nitric acid neutralizes aluminum hydroxide? 3HNO~3~(aq) + Al(OH)~3~(s) $\rightarrow$ ? + 3H~2~O(l)

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ H~2~O\
b)\ AlNO~3~\
c)\ Al(NO~3~)~3~\
d)\ Al(OH)~3~\
e)\ Al~3~NO~3~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**4.** In the reaction HNO~3~(aq) + NaOH(aq) $\rightarrow$ NaNO~3~(aq) + H~2~O(l), which ions are **spectator ions**?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ H^+^ and NO~3~^−^\
b)\ There are no spectator ions in an acid–base reaction\
c)\ Na^+^ and OH^−^\
d)\ Na^+^ and NO~3~^−^\
e)\ H^+^ and OH^−^

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**5.** When the equation below is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients, what is the coefficient of water?

\_\_ HNO~3~(aq) + \_\_ Ca(OH)~2~(aq) $\rightarrow$ \_\_ Ca(NO~3~)~2~(aq) + \_\_ H~2~O(l)

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 1\
b)\ 2\
c)\ 3\
d)\ 4\
e)\ 6

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**6.** Which reaction involves a **transfer of electrons**?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ N~2~(g) + O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2NO(g)\
b)\ AgNO~3~(aq) + KCl(aq) $\rightarrow$ AgCl(s) + KNO~3~(aq)\
c)\ K~2~CO~3~(aq) + 2HCl(aq) $\rightarrow$ 2KCl(aq) + H~2~O(l) + CO~2~(g)\
d)\ NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) $\rightarrow$ NaCl(aq) + H~2~O(l)\
e)\ MgCO~3~(s) $\rightarrow$ MgO(s) + CO~2~(g)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**7.** In the reaction 4Na(s) + O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2Na~2~O(s), how many electrons does **each sodium atom** lose?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0\
b)\ 1\
c)\ 2\
d)\ 3\
e)\ 4

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**8.** In Zn(s) + CuSO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ ZnSO~4~(aq) + Cu(s), which species **gains** electrons?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Zn^2+^\
b)\ SO~4~^2−^\
c)\ No species; no electrons are transferred\
d)\ Zn\
e)\ Cu^2+^

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**9.** When sodium reacts with chlorine, 2Na(s) + Cl~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2NaCl(s), what happens?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Na and Cl share electrons equally and form NaCl molecules\
b)\ Each Na atom loses two electrons\
c)\ Each Cl atom transfers one electron to a Na atom\
d)\ No electrons move; the atoms just combine\
e)\ Each Na atom transfers one electron to a Cl atom, forming Na^+^ and Cl^−^ ions

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**10.** Classify AgNO~3~(aq) + HCl(aq) $\rightarrow$ AgCl(s) + HNO~3~(aq).

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ oxidation–reduction\
b)\ precipitation (double-displacement)\
c)\ gas evolution\
d)\ single-replacement\
e)\ acid–base

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**11.** Which reaction is a **combustion** reaction?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ N~2~(g) + 3H~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2NH~3~(g)\
b)\ 2H~2~O(l) $\rightarrow$ 2H~2~(g) + O~2~(g)\
c)\ CaO(s) + CO~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ CaCO~3~(s)\
d)\ C~2~H~5~OH(l) + 3O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2CO~2~(g) + 3H~2~O(g)\
e)\ HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) $\rightarrow$ NaCl(aq) + H~2~O(l)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**12.** Hydrogen burns: 2H~2~(g) + O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2H~2~O(l). Which classes apply?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ synthesis, combustion, and oxidation–reduction\
b)\ acid–base, because water forms\
c)\ combustion only\
d)\ decomposition and oxidation–reduction\
e)\ synthesis only

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
